decision_conditions: The proposed change of use from a Class C3 two-bedroom dwellinghouse to a Class C4 HMO for six persons represents a significant and harmful intensification of the site. The use of the property by six unrelated individuals would introduce a markedly higher level of activity than the lawful use, resulting in an over-intensification that would harm the character of the area. The principle of development is therefore considered unacceptable and contrary to Policies DMH 1, DMH 5 and DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020) and the NPPF (2024).

The proposed development, by reasons of its increased number of independent occupiers, would generate materially greater noise, comings and goings, and garden use than the existing C3 dwelling, resulting in unacceptable disturbance to neighbouring residents. The submitted HMO Management Plan does not adequately mitigate these effects. The proposal is contrary to Policies DMH 5 and DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020), Policies D3 and D13 of the London Plan (2021), and Paragraph 135(f) of the NPPF (2024).

The proposed development, by reasons of its inadequate internal communal space (i.e.only 2 kitchen spaces equating to 17.6sqm serving six occupiers and no shared living or dining space), would result in poor functionality, failing to provide adequate internal amenity for the future occupants. Bedrooms 2 and 3, in absence of defensible space, would experience insufficient privacy due to their direct relationship with the communal rear garden. The development therefore fails to provide satisfactory living conditions, contrary to Policies DMH 5, DMHB 11, DMHB 16 and DMHB 18 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020), Policies D3 and D6 of the London Plan (2021) and Paragraph 135(f) of the NPPF (2024).

The proposed development, by reason of its insufficient car parking provision, would lead to overspill parking on the public highway, resulting in increased obstruction, vehicle conflict and associated highway safety risks. No parking stress survey has been submitted to demonstrate that surrounding streets can safely accommodate this additional demand. Furthermore, the proposed cycle storage is unsuitable for a communal residential use, failing to provide inclusive, accessible and policy compliant facilities for all users. The combination of inadequate car parking and substandard cycle parking provision is contrary to Policies DMT 1, DMT 2 and DMT 6 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020), Policies T4, T5 and T6 of the London Plan (2021), and Paragraph 116 of the NPPF (2024).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to all relevant planning legislation, regulations, guidance, circulars and Council policies, including The Human Rights Act (1998) (HRA 1998) which makes it unlawful for the Council to act incompatibly with Convention rights, specifically Article 6 (right to a fair hearing); Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life); Article 1 of the First Protocol (protection of property) and Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to the policies and proposals in the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Part 2 (2020) set out below, including Supplementary Planning Guidance, and to all relevant material considerations, including The London Plan (2021) and national guidance.
description: Change of use from Use Class C3 (dwellinghouse) to Use Class C4, to form a six-bedroom, six-person House in Multiple Occupation (HMO) with cycle store. Erection of a single storey extension to the rear, conversion of roof space to habitable use to include a rear dormer
